title: Japan: 20 Days of Adventure, Culture & Feasting: Tokyo → Nikko → Hakone → Takayama → Kanazawa → Kyoto → Nara → Osaka → Hiroshima → Miyajima → Naoshima → Koya-san
description: A sweeping 20-day journey across Japan — from neon-lit Tokyo to misty mountain temples, hidden sake breweries, island art museums, and the best street food on Earth. Designed for two adventurous foodies who want to go deep.

activities.name: Land at Narita/Haneda
activities.description: Pick up your JR Pass at the airport exchange office. Take the Narita Express or monorail to Shinjuku. Check into hotel.
details: Activate JR Pass for Day 2 — don't waste Day 1 on it if arriving late

activities.name: Omoide Yokochō (Memory Lane)
activities.description: Squeeze into a 6-seat yakitori stall in this atmospheric alley of smoke and lanterns. Order everything the chef recommends.
details: Look for stalls with locals — skip ones with English menus outside
Try negima (chicken thigh and leek) and tebasaki (wings)

activities.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Crawl
activities.description: The inner market moved to Toyosu but the outer market is where the magic lives. Eat your way through tamagoyaki, fresh uni, grilled scallops, and strawberry daifuku.
details: Arrive by 7:30am for the best selection
Must-try: Tsukiji Sushiko for a quick nigiri set

activities.name: Ginza Stroll
activities.description: Tokyo's upscale boulevard. Window-shop luxury brands, visit the massive Uniqlo flagship, or duck into the free Sony showroom. Multi-floor arcades, retro game shops, maid cafés, and anime everything. Even if you're not into otaku culture, the energy is wild.
details: Try a crane game — it's a legit skill here

activities.name: Senso-ji Temple
activities.description: Tokyo's oldest temple (628 AD). Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon gate, browse Nakamise-dōri for traditional snacks and souvenirs. Get there early to beat crowds.
details: Free entry · Open 24h but shops open ~9am
Try melon pan and ningyo-yaki from the stalls

activities.name: teamLab Borderless (Azabudai Hills)
activities.description: Immersive digital art that reacts to your movement. Plan 2-3 hours. Book tickets in advance — they sell out.
details: Wear white clothing for best photo effects

activities.name: Shibuya Crossing & Scramble
activities.description: Watch the world's busiest intersection from Starbucks above, then walk through it yourself. Pure Tokyo energy. Shibuya's hidden drinkard's alley — tiny bars seating 4-8 people. Pick one and make friends.

activities.name: Meiji Jingū Shrine
activities.description: Walk through the towering torii gate into a 170-acre forest in the heart of Tokyo. Serene, grounding, and massive. Write a wish on an ema board. Kawaii culture ground zero — rainbow cotton candy, crepe shops, vintage stores. Wild people-watching.
details: Free entry · Open sunrise to sunset
The iris garden is spectacular in May

activities.name: Shimokitazawa Neighborhood Walk
activities.description: Tokyo's coolest neighborhood. Vintage clothing shops, tiny cafés, vinyl record stores, and live music venues. Anti-Shibuya energy — relaxed, creative, local.
details: Stop at Bear Pond for the world's best espresso (weekends only)

activities.name: Tōshō-gū Shrine
activities.description: Wildly ornate mausoleum of Tokugawa Ieyasu. Gold leaf, intricate carvings, the famous 'see no evil' monkeys. Unlike anything else in Japan. Less crowded than Tōshō-gū but equally stunning. The path through ancient cryptomeria trees is magical.
details: JR Pass covers the train to Nikkō (2h from Shinjuku via JR)

activities.name: Kegon Falls
activities.description: 97-meter waterfall fed by Lake Chūzenji. Take the elevator down to the observation deck for the full force of it. One of Japan's top three waterfalls.
details: Bus from Nikkō station (40 min) · Elevator ¥570
tips: Nikkō in May has fresh green canopy and fewer crowds than autumn. The cryptomeria avenue is otherworldly.

activities.name: Hakone Open-Air Museum
activities.description: Stunning outdoor sculpture park with Picasso pavilion. Art set against mountain backdrops. One of Japan's best museums. Switchback mountain railway through lush gorges. The journey IS the attraction.
details: The foot onsen inside is a hidden gem

activities.name: Ōwakudani Volcanic Valley
activities.description: Active sulfur vents, bubbling pools, and the famous black eggs boiled in volcanic hot springs (said to add 7 years to your life). Kitsch but fun — a pirate-themed ferry across the scenic lake with Fuji views on clear days.
details: Cable car from Gōra · ¥1,500 round trip

activities.name: Ryokan Stay with Private Onsen
activities.description: Check into a traditional ryokan in Hakone-Yumoto or Gōra. Kaiseki dinner included — multi-course seasonal perfection. Soak in the private outdoor bath.

days.title: Hakone to Matsumoto — Alpine Castle Town

activities.name: Shinkansen + Limited Express
activities.description: Hakone → Odawara → Nagoya/Matsumoto route. About 3.5 hours total. JR Pass covers it all.

activities.name: Matsumoto Castle
activities.description: One of Japan's five original castles — the 'Crow Castle' with its striking black exterior against the Alps. Climb the steep stairs to the top for panoramic views. Charming merchant streets with sake breweries, craft shops, and frog statues everywhere (the frog is Matsumoto's mascot).
details: One of only 12 original-construction castles in Japan

activities.name: Miyagawa Morning Market
activities.description: Riverside market where local farmers sell pickles, miso, crafts, and mountain vegetables. One of Japan's best morning markets — operating since the Edo period. Second morning market by the old government house. Smaller but equally charming.
details: Buy local hōba miso paste as a souvenir

activities.name: Sanmachi Suji Historic District
activities.description: Three streets of perfectly preserved Edo-era merchant houses. Sake breweries marked by sugidama (cedar balls), traditional crafts, and quiet beauty. 2km temple trail on the eastern hillside. 13 temples and shrines connected by a peaceful path through the forest.
details: Free to walk · Individual breweries offer tastings ¥200-500

activities.name: Nōhi Bus from Takayama
activities.description: 50-minute bus ride through stunning mountain scenery. Book the bus in advance — seats are limited.
details: Not covered by JR Pass — pay separately

activities.name: Ogimachi Village Walk
activities.description: UNESCO World Heritage gasshō-zukuri farmhouses with steep thatched roofs designed to handle heavy snow. Some are 250+ years old and still inhabited. Enter two of the largest farmhouses to see the ingenious multi-story interiors where families lived upstairs and silkworms were raised in the attic.
details: Shiroyama Viewpoint for the classic photo — 15 min uphill walk

activities.name: Bus to Kanazawa
activities.description: 75-minute bus to Kanazawa, the cultural gem of the Sea of Japan coast.

activities.name: Ōmichō Market
activities.description: Kanazawa's kitchen — 200+ stalls of Sea of Japan seafood. Snow crab legs, uni, fat sweet shrimp, and kaisendon (seafood bowls). One of Japan's three great gardens. Meticulously landscaped ponds, streams, bridges, and teahouses. May means vivid green and irises.
details: Open 9am-5pm · Some stalls have eat-in counters

activities.name: Higashi Chaya District
activities.description: Beautifully preserved geisha teahouse district. Wooden lattice buildings, gold leaf ice cream, and quiet elegance. Visit Shima teahouse (¥500) to go inside. Earthen walls and samurai residences. Visit the Nomura Samurai House — its tiny garden was rated one of the top three in Japan by a US journal.

days.title: Kanazawa to Kyoto — Shinkansen & First Night

activities.name: 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art
activities.description: Free zones with the famous 'Swimming Pool' installation by Leandro Erlich. Circular building with playful, accessible art.

activities.name: Hokuriku Shinkansen to Kyoto
activities.description: 2.5 hours through mountain tunnels and rice paddies. Grab an ekiben (train bento) for the ride.
details: JR Pass covered · Unreserved seats fine

activities.name: Pontocho Alley
activities.description: Kyoto's most atmospheric dining lane — one person wide, lantern-lit, packed with restaurants overlooking the Kamo River. In May, outdoor terraces (kawadoko) open. Wander through the geisha district at dusk. Wooden machiya townhouses, stone streets, and if you're lucky, a glimpse of a maiko (apprentice geisha).
details: Be respectful — no chasing or blocking geisha for photos

activities.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
activities.description: 10,000 vermillion torii gates winding up Mt. Inari. Start by 6:30am to have the lower gates nearly to yourself. The full hike takes 2-3 hours round trip.
details: Most tourists only do the first 20 min — keep going for the magic

activities.name: Kiyomizu-dera Temple
activities.description: Iconic wooden stage jutting out over the hillside — built without a single nail. Stunning views over Kyoto. The approach streets (Ninenzaka, Sannenzaka) are beautiful. Picturesque stone-paved lanes lined with tea houses, pottery shops, and traditional sweets. Very photogenic.

activities.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
activities.description: Walk through towering bamboo stalks that creak and sway overhead. Arrive by 7am for an empty path. The sound alone is worth it. Hike 20 minutes up the hill to hang out with 120 wild macaques with panoramic views of Kyoto. You're in THEIR space.
details: Free · Always open · Near Saga-Arashiyama Station

activities.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
activities.description: The gold-leaf-covered pavilion reflected in its mirror pond. Iconic for a reason. Late afternoon light is best for photos. Japan's most famous zen rock garden — 15 stones in raked gravel. No matter where you sit, you can only see 14 at once. Meditative and profound.

days.title: Kyoto Deep Dive — Sake, Tea & Hidden Temples

activities.name: Fushimi Sake Brewery Walk
activities.description: Kyoto's brewing heartland — Gekkeikan, Kizakura, and smaller craft breweries along a canal lined with willows. Tastings everywhere.
details: Buy a cup for ¥400 and fill it at different breweries

activities.name: Uji — Birthplace of Japanese Tea
activities.description: 20 minutes from Kyoto by train. The town where matcha culture began. Byōdō-in Temple (the one on the ¥10 coin) and tea shops everywhere.
details: Byōdō-in ¥700 · Nakamura Tokichi for the best matcha experience

activities.name: Daitoku-ji Zen Compound
activities.description: Complex of 20+ sub-temples, most hidden behind walls. Kōtō-in has a famous maple approach. Zuihō-in has a hidden Christian rock garden. Tourist-free zen.

activities.name: Nara Park & Deer
activities.description: 1,200+ sacred deer roam freely. Buy deer crackers (¥200) and bow to them — they bow back. Some are pushy, most are adorable. Houses the world's largest bronze Buddha (15m tall) inside the world's largest wooden building. The scale is jaw-dropping even after photos.

activities.name: Kasuga Taisha Shrine
activities.description: 3,000 stone and bronze lanterns line the path through a primeval forest. Twice a year they're all lit — but even unlit, it's magical. Preserved merchant quarter with machiya townhouses converted into cafés, galleries, and mochi shops. Quieter and more charming than Kyoto's equivalents.

activities.name: Kuromon Market (Osaka's Kitchen)
activities.description: Covered market with 170+ stalls. Graze through fresh uni, ōtoro tuna, grilled king crab legs, and tamagoyaki.
details: Go hungry — this is a 2-hour eating marathon

activities.name: Dōtonbori Walk
activities.description: Osaka's neon heart — the giant Glico running man, mechanical crab, and more takoyaki shops than you can count. Pure sensory overload. Retro Osaka at its most lovable. Kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers) joints everywhere. No double-dipping in the communal sauce — that's the ONE rule.

activities.name: Amerikamura & Ura-Namba
activities.description: Osaka's cool neighborhoods. Amerikamura for vinyl and streetwear, Ura-Namba for hidden standing bars and yakitori joints.

activities.name: Osaka Castle
activities.description: Towering reconstructed castle surrounded by a massive park and moat. The museum inside covers Toyotomi Hideyoshi's rise. Best views from the outer walls.
details: The surrounding park is free and great for a morning walk

activities.name: Nakazakichō
activities.description: Hidden neighborhood of converted prewar houses — now tiny cafés, vintage shops, and galleries. Osaka's most underrated area. Osaka-style okonomiyaki (savory pancake) at Mizuno near Dōtonbori — Michelin-recognized, made right in front of you on a teppan.
details: Near Nakazakichō Station · Free to explore

activities.name: Shinkansen to Hiroshima
activities.description: 80 minutes from Osaka on the Sakura shinkansen. JR Pass covered. Deeply moving. The museum, A-Bomb Dome, Children's Peace Monument, and eternal flame. Allow 2 hours minimum. It will change you.
details: The paper crane displays are heartbreaking and hopeful

activities.name: Ferry to Miyajima
activities.description: JR Ferry from Miyajimaguchi (covered by JR Pass). 10-minute ride to the sacred island. The iconic vermillion torii gate 'floating' in the sea at high tide. At low tide, walk out to it. UNESCO World Heritage.
details: Check tide times — both high and low tide are beautiful in different ways

activities.name: Shinkansen to Okayama, then Ferry
activities.description: Hiroshima → Okayama (40 min shinkansen), then bus to Uno Port, ferry to Naoshima (20 min). Arrive by late morning.
details: Rent bikes at the port — best way to explore the island

activities.name: Benesse House Museum
activities.description: Art museum designed by Tadao Ando, built into a hillside overlooking the Inland Sea. Monets, Hirsts, and site-specific installations in concrete perfection. Built entirely underground to preserve the landscape. Three artists only: Monet, James Turrell, Walter De Maria. The Turrell light installation will stop you in your tracks.

activities.name: Naoshima → Kōya-san
activities.description: Ferry back to Uno, train to Osaka/Namba, then Nankai Railway + cable car to Kōya-san. A journey, but the arrival is worth every minute.
details: About 4-5 hours total · Nankai line not covered by JR Pass (¥2,500)

activities.name: Okunoin Cemetery Walk
activities.description: 2km path through Japan's largest cemetery — 200,000+ tombstones under ancient cedar trees. Moss-covered stone lanterns, corporate memorials from Toyota and Panasonic, and the mausoleum of Kōbō Daishi at the end. Profoundly peaceful. Stunning vermillion pagoda and temple complex — the center of Shingon Buddhism founded in 816 AD.
details: Free · Open 24/7 — nighttime walk is extraordinary

activities.name: Overnight at a Shukubō
activities.description: Sleep in a Buddhist temple — futons on tatami, shōjin ryōri (vegetarian monk cuisine) dinner and breakfast, optional 6am morning prayer chanting. The perfect ending to 20 days in Japan.
details: Morning prayer at 6am is optional but unforgettable
